question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

D, A, V, S, N, ?, F, C
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. K.

GIVEN

• D, A, V, S, N, ?, F, C

SOLUTION

• Take letter positions (A=1 … Z=26) and read the differences: the series alternates −3, −5, −3, −5 …

• D(4) −3→ A(1) −5→ V(22) −3→ S(19) −5→ N(14) −3→ ? −5→ F(6) −3→ C(3).

• 14 − 3 = 11 = K; check next: 11 − 5 = 6 = F ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just apply the fixed cycle −3, −5 from D onward; the 6th term is 14−3 = 11 = K.

NOTE

• In backward letter series, convert to numbers and subtract using mod-26 (if value ≤0, add 26).

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and third letter cluster is related to fourth letter cluster.

DPT : IUY :: ICR : NHW :: ? : SXP
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. NSK.

GIVEN

• DPT : IUY :: ICR : NHW :: ? : SXP

SOLUTION

• First→second cluster: each letter +5. D+5=I, P+5=U, T+5=Y ✓ and I+5=N, C+5=H, R+5=W ✓.

• So the missing cluster = SXP −5 on each letter: S(19)−5=N, X(24)−5=S, P(16)−5=K → NSK.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The rule is +5 forward; to get the first cluster, move SXP back by 5 → NSK.

NOTE

• When the pair goes forward by k, the unknown first term is the second term shifted back by k.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AM, XI, ?, RA, OW, LS, IO, FK
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. UE.

GIVEN

• AM, XI, ?, RA, OW, LS, IO, FK

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: A(1), X(24), ?, R(18), O(15), L(12), I(9), F(6) → decreasing by 3: 1, 24, 21, 18… so ? = 21 = U.

• 2nd letters: M(13), I(9), ?, A(1), W(23), S(19), O(15), K(11) → decreasing by 4: 13, 9, 5… so ? = 5 = E.

• Missing term = UE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Two parallel chains: first letters −3, second letters −4. Third term = 21U + 5E = UE.

NOTE

• Split each cluster into separate column-series; solve each column independently.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(KF, IC, GZ)

(FW, DT, BQ)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (QY, OV, MS).

GIVEN

• (KF, IC, GZ) and (FW, DT, BQ)

SOLUTION

• Across the three clusters of a set: 1st letters fall by 2, 2nd letters fall by 3.

• KF→IC→GZ: K,I,G (−2) and F,C,Z (−3) ✓. FW→DT→BQ: F,D,B (−2) and W,T,Q (−3) ✓.

• Option: QY→OV→MS: Q,O,M (−2) and Y,V,S (−3) ✓ — same rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check only the step between clusters: (−2, −3). Only (QY, OV, MS) fits both columns.

NOTE

• For a 'set that follows the same rule' question, compare column-wise gaps, not letters inside one cluster.

question: What will be the sum of number of Sundays in the months of March and December of 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 10.

GIVEN

• Year 2019 (ordinary year); count Sundays in March and December.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2019 = Tuesday. 1 March = Tuesday + (31+28=59, 59 mod 7 = 3) = Friday; so Sundays fall on 3,10,17,24,31 → 5 Sundays.

• 1 Dec = Tuesday + (334 mod 7 = 5) = Sunday; so Sundays on 1,8,15,22,29 → 5 Sundays.

• Sum = 5 + 5 = 10.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month has 5 of whichever 3 weekdays it starts with; both months start on a day that makes Sunday a 5th-occurrence → 5 + 5 = 10.

NOTE

• Any month with 31 days gives 5 occurrences to its first 3 weekdays; 30-day to first 2; Feb(28) exactly 4 each.

question:
In the year 1910, which of the following month had 5 Thursdays?

I. March

II. May
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Only I.

GIVEN

• Year 1910 (ordinary year); check 5 Thursdays in March and May.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 1910 = Saturday (1 Jan 1900 was Monday; +12 odd days in 10 yrs → Saturday).

• 1 March = Sat + (59 mod 7 = 3) = Tuesday; 31-day month → 5 each of Tue, Wed, Thu ⇒ March has 5 Thursdays ✓ (I true).

• 1 May = Sat + (120 mod 7 = 1) = Sunday; 31-day month → 5 each of Sun, Mon, Tue; Thursday only 4 times (II false).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The extra 3 days of a 31-day month are its starting weekday and the next two; only if Thursday is among them does it occur 5 times.

NOTE

• Anchor: 1 Jan 1900 = Monday; add (years + leap-years) odd days to reach any date.

question: Height of 5 students J, K, L, M and N is compared. Height of no two students is same. Height of K is shorter than L but taller than J. Height of no one is shorter than N. L is not the tallest among them. How many students have height less than L but more than N?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• J < K < L; no one shorter than N (N is shortest); L is not the tallest.

SOLUTION

• Since L is not tallest, the only remaining student M must be taller than L → M > L.

• N is the shortest, so N < J. Full order (tall→short): M > L > K > J > N.

• Students shorter than L but taller than N = K and J = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Build one chain M > L > K > J > N; count names strictly between L and N → 2.

NOTE

• 'No one is shorter than N' = N is the minimum; 'not the tallest' pushes the leftover person to the top.

question: 7 girls G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6 and G7 are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). G4 is not next to G6. G2 is not next to G1. G6 is second to the left of G3. G1 is third to the right of G3. G7 is third to the right of G6. Considering towards left of G4, how many girls are sitting between G4 and G6?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 7 girls, circular, facing OUTWARD (so right = clockwise, left = anticlockwise).

SOLUTION

• Fix G6 at a seat. G6 is 2nd to left of G3 → G3 = G6 + 2 (clockwise). G7 = G6 + 3. G1 = G3 + 3 = G6 + 5.

• Clockwise seats (0–6): G6=0, G3=2, G7=3, G1=5. Remaining 1, 4, 6 for G2, G4, G5.

• G4 not next to G6 → G4 ≠ 1, 6 → G4 = 4. G2 not next to G1(5) → G2 ≠ 6 → G2 = 1, G5 = 6.

• Order: G6, G2, G3, G7, G4, G1, G5. Going left (anticlockwise) from G4: G7, G3, G2, then G6 → 3 girls in between.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Place fixed clues from G6, fill gaps with the 'not-next-to' rules, then just count seats between G4 and G6 on the required side.

NOTE

• Facing outward reverses left/right versus facing centre — apply that before plotting.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. a square with a hexagon holding a smaller hexagon and a central dot.

GIVEN

• 1st pair: square-with-diamond → square-with-diamond-inside-diamond + central dot. Then square-with-hexagon : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: the inner shape is repeated once more inside itself and a dot is placed at the centre.

• Applying to the hexagon: hexagon gets a smaller hexagon inside it plus a central dot.

• That is exactly Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The inner figure must stay the SAME type (hexagon). Options 1 (circle) and 4 (outer circle) and 2 (heptagon) change the shape → reject; only Option keeps a hexagon-in-hexagon + dot.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, first identify the transformation, then eliminate options that alter shape identity.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with 2 on top, 1 7 3 in the middle row and 5 at the bottom.

GIVEN

• 1st box (top/left-mid/right/bottom, centre) → 2nd box under one rule. Third box: top 1, middle 5 4 2, bottom 3.

SOLUTION

• Position rule (box1→box2): Top ← old Mid-Right, Mid-Left ← old Top, Mid-Right ← old Bottom, Bottom ← old Mid-Left; centre number +3.

• Apply to box3 (Top 1, ML 5, centre 4, MR 2, Bottom 3): Top = 2, ML = 1, MR = 3, Bottom = 5, centre = 4+3 = 7.

• Result: Top 2 / row 1 7 3 / bottom 5 = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The centre always becomes +3 (4→7); only options with a 7 in the centre survive → Option.

NOTE

• Track each spatial slot separately (rotation of outer items + arithmetic on the centre).

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

QF20 : RH40 :: LX15 : MZ30 :: GP12 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HR24.

GIVEN

• QF20 : RH40 :: LX15 : MZ30 :: GP12 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: 1st letter +1, 2nd letter +2, number ×2.

• Check: Q+1=R, F+2=H, 20×2=40 ✓; L+1=M, X+2=Z, 15×2=30 ✓.

• GP12: G+1=H, P+2=R, 12×2=24 → HR24.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters +1/+2, number doubles → H, R, 24.

NOTE

• Solve letters and number by independent, consistent operations; verify on both given pairs first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

ADJ120 : NHE280 :: RKI130 : MOV290 :: LVT160 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. XZP320.

GIVEN

• ADJ120 : NHE280 :: RKI130 : MOV290 :: LVT160 : ?

SOLUTION

• Letter rule: reverse the three letters, then add 4 to each. Number rule: +160.

• ADJ → reverse JDA → +4 → N,H,E = NHE ✓ (120+160=280). RKI → IKR → +4 → M,O,V = MOV ✓ (130+160=290).

• LVT → reverse TVL → +4 → X(24), Z(26), P(16) = XZP; 160+160 = 320 → XZP320.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the letters, shift each +4, add 160 to the number → XZP320.

NOTE

• If a direct per-position shift is inconsistent, test 'reverse then shift' — a very common SSC twist.

question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Discriminate

2. Discrepancy

3. Discreet

4. Discredit

5. Discuss
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 43215.

GIVEN

• 1.Discriminate 2.Discrepancy 3.Discreet 4.Discredit 5.Discuss

SOLUTION

• Common start 'Discr…'. Compare 6th letter: Discredit, Discreet, Discrepancy → order d < e < p → 4, 3, 2.

• Then Discriminate ('Discri…', i > e) comes next → 1. Finally Discuss ('Discu…', u > r) is last → 5.

• Sequence = 4, 3, 2, 1, 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• All share 'Discr'; rank by the next differing letter: d<e<p<(i)…, and 'Discu' goes to the very end.

NOTE

• Compare letter-by-letter from the first point of difference; earlier alphabet letter comes first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

5077 : 5034 :: 1558 : ? :: 3323 : 3280
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1515.

GIVEN

• 5077 : 5034 :: 1558 : ? :: 3323 : 3280

SOLUTION

• Rule: subtract 43. 5077 − 43 = 5034 ✓; 3323 − 43 = 3280 ✓.

• 1558 − 43 = 1515.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference of −43 across all pairs → 1558 − 43 = 1515.

NOTE

• When two model pairs share the same gap, apply that same gap to the unknown pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

871 : 550 :: 397 : ? :: 630 : 309

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 76.

question: In a certain coded language 'BUCK' is coded as 'DYZF' and 'FLOW' is coded as 'HPLR'. How will 'HANK' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JEKF.

GIVEN

• BUCK → DYZF, FLOW → HPLR.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts: 1st +2, 2nd +4, 3rd −3, 4th −5.

• Check: B+2=D, U+4=Y, C−3=Z, K−5=F ✓; F+2=H, L+4=P, O−3=L, W−5=R ✓.

• HANK: H+2=J, A+4=E, N−3=K, K−5=F → JEKF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift pattern +2, +4, −3, −5 applied to H, A, N, K gives J, E, K, F.

NOTE

• Derive the per-letter shift from the given words, then apply the same shifts by position.

question: At what time (in PM), the angle between hour and minute hands of a clock will be 100 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7:20.

GIVEN

• Find the time whose hour–minute angle is exactly 100°.

SOLUTION

• Angle = |30H − 5.5M|.

• 7:20 → |30×7 − 5.5×20| = |210 − 110| = 100° ✓.

• Others: 6:15 = 97.5°, 1:55 = 87.5°, 3:00 = 90° — none is 100°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Plug each option into |30H − 5.5M|; only 7:20 gives 100.

NOTE

• Hour hand moves 30°/hr = 0.5°/min; minute hand 6°/min; hence the |30H − 5.5M| formula.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with 5 vertical lines and a hollow (unfilled) small square at the bottom-right.

GIVEN

• Fig1: 1 line, hollow square bottom-right. Fig2: 2 lines, filled square bottom-left. Fig3: 3 lines, hollow bottom-right. Fig4: 4 lines, filled bottom-left.

SOLUTION

• The number of top vertical lines increases 1, 2, 3, 4 → next is 5.

• The corner square alternates: hollow-bottom-right, filled-bottom-left, … so the 5th figure = hollow square, bottom-right.

• That matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd positions = hollow square bottom-right; 5 is odd → hollow, bottom-right, with 5 lines → Option.

NOTE

• Track each feature (count, fill, position) as an independent alternating/increasing pattern.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with top row G H K, then F, then J.

GIVEN

• Fig1: (F G H / J / K), Fig2: (J F G / K / H), Fig3: (K J F / H / G), Fig4: (H K J / G / F).

SOLUTION

• Each step the five letters cycle through fixed slots: new-Top1 = old-Middle, top row otherwise shifts right, old-top-right drops to Bottom, old-Bottom rises to Middle.

• Applying to Fig4 (H K J / G / F): Top row = G H K, Middle = F, Bottom = J → (G H K / F / J).

• That is Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the top-left letters down the series: F, J, K, H, → G next; the full box then reads G H K / F / J.

NOTE

• Treat the box as fixed positions and follow where each letter migrates each step.

question: The present ages of A and B is 11 years and 15 years respectively. What was the ratio of ages of A and B, 6 years ago?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5 : 9.

GIVEN

• Present ages: A = 11 years, B = 15 years.

SOLUTION

• 6 years ago: A = 11 − 6 = 5, B = 15 − 6 = 9.

• Ratio = 5 : 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 6 from each present age and write the ratio → 5 : 9.

NOTE

• 'x years ago' means subtract x from every present age before forming the ratio.
